links.reason: Fate gets there before any plan to beat it, yet those who strive without faltering are promised they will see its back.
links.quoteA: What is stronger than fate?
links.quoteB: will see the back of fate itself

links.reason: What fate denies won’t stay however you guard it, yet effort pays the wages of your toil even if god won’t allow it.
links.quoteA: What isn’t yours by fate won’t stay
links.quoteB: Even if god won’t allow it, effort pays the wages

links.reason: The fate that takes wealth away brings laziness, yet making no effort is called your own disgrace, not fate’s.
links.quoteA: The fate that takes it away brings laziness
links.quoteB: The disgrace is to know what must be known and make no effort

links.reason: Austerity is striven for because it brings what you want as you want it, yet craving can never be filled and is to be given up.
links.quoteA: what you want comes as you want it
links.quoteB: If you give up craving, whose nature is never to be filled

links.reason: The highest wisdom does no evil even to those who hate you, yet austerity is held out as a power that can crush enemies, if you wish it.
links.quoteA: do no evil even to those who hate you
links.quoteB: Crushing enemies and raising those who are dear: if you wish it, austerity can do both

links.reason: Those on the hill called virtue have an anger hard to withstand, yet renouncing anger is what makes you the equal of renouncers.
links.quoteA: The anger of those who stand on the hill called virtue is hard to withstand
links.quoteB: Those who renounce anger are the equals of renouncers

links.reason: Those who wrong you in pride are to be conquered by nobility; fail to humble such pride, says the other, and you will not last.
links.quoteA: Conquer by thy nobility those that in their pride have injured thee
links.quoteB: they shall not last long, those who humble not the pride of men who defy them

links.reason: Think how you stand before the strong before you go against the weak, says one; the other tells you to seek enmity with the weak without holding back.
links.quoteA: When you go against those weaker than you, think of yourself before those stronger
links.quoteB: Without holding back, seek enmity with the weak

links.reason: Someone who prizes anger will surely be ruined, yet the wise are shown burning within and watching for their time.
links.quoteA: Someone who prizes anger will be ruined
links.quoteB: They watch for the time and burn within

links.reason: Uprightness and shame come by nature only to those of good family, yet birth is the same for all and only what they do sets them apart.
links.quoteA: Only in those born of a good family do uprightness and shame come together by nature
links.quoteB: Birth is the same for every living being

links.reason: He calls a woman’s restraint under ocean-deep passion her grandeur; she answers that such self-respect is unknown to the lovesick.
links.quoteA: the woman who refuseth to ride the palm-stalk
links.quoteB: a thing unknown to the lovesick fair

links.reason: No one is crueller than those who live by deceit as if they had renounced, yet a spy is praised for taking that very form.
links.quoteA: those who don’t renounce in their hearts but live by deceit, as if they had renounced
links.quoteB: A spy takes the form of those who have renounced

links.reason: A heart free of falsehood wins every heart, yet with a foe you cannot yet break from, you are told to feign friendship.
links.quoteA: Live without lying in your heart
links.quoteB: be friends with the face, and put friendship out of the heart

links.reason: Nothing at all is better than truthfulness, says one, yet the other ranks not killing first and puts not lying second.
links.quoteA: nothing at all is better than truthfulness
links.quoteB: Not killing stands alone as good. Next after it, not lying is good

links.reason: Compassion is the wealth above all wealth, and goods are found even among the low, yet compassion is said to thrive with wealth as its foster-mother.
links.quoteA: The wealth of compassion is the wealth among wealth
links.quoteB: thrives with the rich foster-mother called wealth

links.reason: Wealth by its nature doesn’t stay, yet it is also called an unfailing lamp that goes to whatever land you think of.
links.quoteA: It is the nature of wealth not to stay
links.quoteB: The unfailing lamp called wealth

links.reason: The one who lives home life well is first among all who strive, yet those who renounce completely have arrived and all others are caught in a net.
links.quoteA: The one who lives home life as it should be lived is first among all who strive
links.quoteB: All others are deluded, and caught in a net

links.reason: Ruin from helping others is worth buying, even if you must sell up, yet you are also told to give knowing your limit and to look after your wealth.
links.quoteA: that ruin is worth buying, even if you must sell up to do it
links.quoteB: Give in the right way, knowing your limit

links.reason: Not killing is what righteous action is, yet a ruler who punishes the wicked with death is likened to someone pulling weeds from a green crop.
links.quoteA: What is righteous action? Not killing
links.quoteB: A ruler who punishes the wicked with death is like someone pulling weeds from a green crop

links.reason: Begging from those who hide nothing is like giving, says one chapter; the next says not begging is worth ten million times more, even there.
links.quoteA: Begging is like giving
links.quoteB: not begging is worth ten million times more

links.reason: Without people who beg the world would be a wooden puppet; the next chapter curses its maker if anyone must live by begging.
links.quoteA: Without people who beg, this great cool world would be a wooden puppet
links.quoteB: wanted people to live even by begging, let him wander far and perish

links.reason: Bow to your adversaries until they decline, says one; in your own decline, says the other, hold fast to your dignity.
links.quoteA: Bend down before thy adversaries
links.quoteB: in the day of thy decline hold fast to thy dignity

links.reason: A lack of understanding is called the worst poverty and no other lack counts, yet the other answers that only poverty hurts like poverty.
links.quoteA: The world does not count any other lack as poverty
links.quoteB: Only poverty hurts like poverty

links.reason: Those of an old family keep their good nature when their means shrink, yet poverty brings even them a weakness from which shameful words are born.
links.quoteA: those of an old family don’t part from their good nature
links.quoteB: Even in those of good family, poverty brings a weakness

links.reason: Loss will always come, and only a heart that doesn’t lean sets the worthy apart, yet those who hold to compassion are said to have no misery.
links.quoteA: Loss and gain will always come
links.quoteB: Those who hold to compassion have no misery

links.reason: Only killing the good done to you leaves no escape, says one; the other says no one escapes their own deed, which follows them and kills.
links.quoteA: Those who have killed any good may still escape
links.quoteB: The enemy that is your own deed never goes away

links.reason: A single evil word turns all your good bad, yet the noble may say things without goodness, so long as they say nothing useless.
links.quoteA: If a single evil word does its harm, the good you have done turns bad
links.quoteB: Let the noble say things without goodness if they will

links.reason: The one at a ruler’s side must tell him what is good for him, however he takes it, yet those around him are told to say what isn’t disliked, and to please.
links.quoteA: it is the duty of the one at his side to tell him what is good for him
links.quoteB: say what is needed and not disliked, in a way that pleases

links.reason: Desire grown full leaves no room for a sulk, she says; he says sulking is sweet with those who love you.
links.quoteA: you must not sulk even by a millet seed
links.quoteB: sulking is sweet with those who love you

links.reason: Remembering their days together is how she stays alive, yet keeping him in her heart, she says later, will only cost her more of her beauty.
links.quoteA: I live by remembering the days I was with him
links.quoteB: If we keep in our heart the one who left us and won’t come near, we will lose still more of our beauty

links.reason: Doting on a wife bars a man from the finest reward, yet the lover asks if even the world of the lotus-eyed one is sweeter than her shoulders.
links.quoteA: Men who dote on their wives won’t win the finest reward
links.quoteB: Is the world of the lotus-eyed one sweeter than sleep on the soft shoulders of the one you love?

links.reason: Many who didn’t know their strength broke halfway, yet all your thoughts are to be of rising higher, since even failing has the nature of not failing.
links.quoteA: set out on a surge of zeal and broke halfway
links.quoteB: Let all your thoughts be of rising higher

links.reason: The wise won’t accept an unlearned man’s cleverness even when it is very good, yet understanding is seeing the reality in what you hear, from anyone.
links.quoteA: Even when an unlearned man’s cleverness is very good, the wise don’t accept it
links.quoteB: Whatever you hear, from whoever’s mouth, understanding is seeing the reality in it

links.reason: For those who hold to friendship there is no leaving it once made, yet with those who spoil your work you are told to let it slowly slip away.
links.quoteA: once made there is no leaving it
links.quoteB: let the friendship slowly slip away

links.reason: People can be red outside and black inside, yet the face, like crystal, is said to show what is strongest in the heart.
links.quoteA: red outside like the crab’s-eye seed, yet black inside
links.quoteB: the face shows what is strongest in the heart

links.reason: The enmity of a man who does a task all wrong is worth paying for, yet the very next chapter says no one should want enmity, even in jest.
links.quoteA: Even if you must pay for it, be sure to get the enmity
links.quoteB: No one should want it, even in jest

links.reason: The sceptre, not the spear, brings a ruler victory, yet an army that fears no wound and wins is ranked first of all his riches.
links.quoteA: It is not the spear that brings a ruler victory. It is the sceptre
links.quoteB: A complete army that fears no wound and wins is the first of all a ruler’s riches

links.reason: A lifetime of good deeds walls up the road to rebirth, yet good deeds too bear pain-engendering fruits from which one must be freed.
links.quoteA: the pain-engendering fruits of action both good and evil
links.quoteB: thou wallest up the road to future births

links.reason: The bond of body and soul is as slight as a bird leaving its shell, yet the lover takes that same bond as the measure of how deep his love runs.
links.quoteA: that is the symbol of the love between the soul and the body
links.quoteB: How great is the love between the body and the soul?

links.reason: Doubting someone you have come to trust brings endless suffering, yet a spy is there to watch everyone alike, even those who do your work and your kin.
links.quoteA: to doubt someone you have come to trust
links.quoteB: those who do your work, your own kin

links.reason: Learning lifts you above others as humans stand above beasts, unless you fear an assembly of the good, when you sink below the unlearned.
links.quoteA: those who have learned and understood, yet fear an assembly of the good, are lower than the unlearned
links.quoteB: As beasts are to humans, so others are to those who have learned bright books

links.reason: Learning alone doesn’t set you above the rest: someone who studies, teaches and still has no self-control is the greatest fool of all.
links.quoteA: No one is a greater fool than someone who studies, understands, teaches others, and still has no self-control
links.quoteB: As beasts are to humans, so others are to those who have learned bright books

links.reason: Bearing with those who scorn you is called the highest thing, but holding back anger only counts where the anger could take effect.
links.quoteA: Whoever holds back anger where it can take effect truly holds it back
links.quoteB: the highest thing is to bear with those who scorn you

links.reason: Humility is called good in everyone, but bowing low belongs to plenty: when your means shrink, you are told to stand tall.
links.quoteA: In plenty, bow low. When your means shrink, stand tall
links.quoteB: Humility is good in everyone

links.reason: Doing good however you can isn’t enough: even good can go wrong if it isn’t done knowing each person’s nature.
links.quoteA: Even doing good can go wrong, if you don’t do it knowing each person’s nature
links.quoteB: do righteous deeds everywhere they can be done

links.reason: Sulking may be the joy of desire, but it is like salt: drawing it out is a little too much.
links.quoteA: Drawing it out is like a little too much
links.quoteB: Sulking is the joy of desire

links.reason: Renown is made the point of appearing at all, but those who want glory with strength of character won’t do anything unworthy even for glory.
links.quoteA: won’t do anything unworthy, even for glory
links.quoteB: If you appear, appear with renown

links.reason: Only kin are said to cherish old ties when you have lost everything, but an enemy within who is close by kinship brings harms that lead towards death.
links.quoteA: When an enemy within appears who is close by kinship, it brings many harms
links.quoteB: Only kin go on cherishing old ties even when you have lost everything

links.reason: Trust is to go to those who pass every test, but many who pass every test still change once they are doing the work.
links.quoteA: many people change with the nature of the work
links.quoteB: Test someone by these four, righteousness, wealth, pleasure and fear for their life, and then trust them

links.reason: The rule to act only after careful deliberation has an exception: when a rare chance comes, do not hesitate.
links.quoteA: do at that very moment what is hard to do
links.quoteB: Think, then commit to the task

links.reason: A ruler’s honour must never slip from valour, but honour that has lost its nobility is itself counted among a ruler’s faults.
links.quoteA: honour that has lost its nobility
links.quoteB: an honour that never slips from valour

links.reason: The elephant firm under arrows does not prove that spirit is enough: stuck in a marsh, that same beast falls to a jackal.
links.quoteA: even a jackal will triumph over him when he is entangled in marshy ground
links.quoteB: the elephant planteth his legs only more firmly

links.reason: Wanting nothing is set above everything: a pride that breeds victory in one, a wealth with no equal here or there in the other.
links.quoteA: The pride of wanting nothing breeds victory
links.quoteB: There is no great wealth here to match wanting nothing

links.reason: A family’s rise rests on refusing to idle, put as treating laziness for what it is in one and as not resting your hands from the work in the other.
links.quoteA: should treat laziness as the laziness it is
links.quoteB: I won’t rest my hands from the work

links.reason: Answer those who harm you by outdoing them in goodness: defeat them by your own worth, or punish them with good that shames them.
links.quoteA: Defeat by your own worth those who wrong you
links.quoteB: do them such good that they are ashamed

links.reason: Good done to the one who harmed you is the answer in each, and the later couplet makes it the very test of worth.
links.quoteA: do them such good that they are ashamed
links.quoteB: What use is worth, if you don’t do kindness even to those who have done you harm?

links.reason: Deliberate injury is no licence: even when someone hurts you out of hate or to pick a quarrel, you do not return it.
links.quoteA: Not harming in return, even when someone has harmed you in hatred
links.quoteB: it is best not to answer with harm out of strife

links.reason: However great the wrong, even one that burns like many fires, the good course is the same: do not be moved to answer it.
links.quoteA: it is good to suffer the pain and do nothing unrighteous
links.quoteB: it is good not to be angry, if you can

links.reason: No necessity excuses a shameful act, not a hungry mother in one nor things you can’t do without in the other.
links.quoteA: Even if you see the mother who bore you go hungry, don’t do what the worthy condemn
links.quoteB: Even things you can’t do without, give them up if they would lower you

links.reason: Anyone who wants to be free of suffering has the same single course in each: do no harm, since harm returns to its doer.
links.quoteA: If you don’t want painful things to strike you down, don’t do evil things to others
links.quoteB: Those who want to be free of pain cause none

links.reason: Evil comes back to those who do it, unprompted: it stays at their feet like a shadow in one and arrives by afternoon, by itself, in the other.
links.quoteA: like a shadow that never leaves, and stays at their feet
links.quoteB: harm will come to you in the afternoon, by itself

links.reason: Turn on your own faults the eye you keep for others’ and no harm can reach you, said first to everyone and later to the ruler.
links.quoteA: If you could see your own faults as you see strangers’ faults
links.quoteB: If a ruler removes his own faults first, and then looks at those of others

links.reason: A high aim that fails beats a low one that succeeds: rising thoughts don’t truly fail, and a spear that missed an elephant outdoes an arrow in a hare.
links.quoteA: Even when it fails, it has the nature of not failing
links.quoteB: Better to hold a spear that missed an elephant than an arrow that hit a hare

links.reason: You can get what you have set your mind on, on one condition stated in each: that you keep your mind on it and stay firm.
links.quoteA: Getting what you have set your mind on is easy, if you can keep your mind on it
links.quoteB: Those who plan will get what they planned, just as they planned it, if they are firm

links.reason: What you offer those who can’t take it is simply lost: ambrosia spilled in a filthy yard, or a lesson that leaves the teacher seeing nothing himself.
links.quoteA: like ambrosia spilled in a filthy yard
links.quoteB: Whoever tries to show a man who can’t see ends up seeing nothing himself

links.reason: A fort is only as good as those in it: there is no fort for those who are afraid, and none for those with no excellence in action.
links.quoteA: There is no fort for those who are afraid
links.quoteB: with those who have no excellence in action it is no fortress

links.reason: A fortress is not only the refuge of the weak: the strong and powerful, each insists, gain just as much from one.
links.quoteA: Even to the strong and warlike, a gain that rests on a stronghold brings many benefits
links.quoteB: A fortress is of value to those who are strong

links.reason: Learning that cannot be put across to others is worthless: a flower without scent in one, good for nothing in the other.
links.quoteA: like flowers that bloom in clusters but have no scent
links.quoteB: of no use, however much they have learned

links.reason: The person worth having is described in nearly the same words, well-born and dreading blame, first as one to trust and then as a friend.
links.quoteA: born of good family, free of faults, and has the shame that dreads a scar
links.quoteB: Someone well-born, who shrinks from blame upon himself

links.reason: Rule stays sound only if the ruler looks into it daily: do so every day, or watch the land go to ruin day by day.
links.quoteA: Let the ruler look into it every day
links.quoteB: When a ruler doesn’t look into things daily and do justice, his land goes to ruin day by day

links.reason: Looks are no measure of a person, shown by the cruel arrow and the bent harp in one and by the axle pin of a great chariot in the other.
links.quoteA: Judge people the same way, by what they do
links.quoteB: Don’t scorn people for how they look

links.reason: No prize justifies a stain on your name: not piled-up millions for those of good family, not the wide world for the best of people.
links.quoteA: Even for piled-up millions, those of good family won’t do anything that lowers them
links.quoteB: won’t want the wide world unless they have shame as their fence

links.reason: Gain made the wrong way is to be let go, however good it looks: give it up at once in one, let it roll away in the other.
links.quoteA: let go at once of gain that comes from leaving the middle
links.quoteB: don’t embrace it, let it roll away

links.reason: Wealth won by stealing or deceit can’t hold, however it seems to grow: it perishes in one, and it is water in a pot of raw clay in the other.
links.quoteA: seems to grow, then perishes beyond all measure
links.quoteB: like pouring water into a pot of raw clay

links.reason: Failing to guard in advance is punished when the blow comes: you are straw before a fire in one, and left regretting it in the other.
links.quoteA: like a stack of straw before a fire
links.quoteB: will regret that mistake when the blow lands

links.reason: Giving trust or friendship without testing is the same mistake with a lasting price: suffering for those after you, or a sorrow that kills.
links.quoteA: Trust a stranger without testing them, and the suffering won’t end
links.quoteB: Someone who makes a friend without looking and looking again ends in a sorrow that kills him

links.reason: Desire outdoes liquor in the same way, heard first from him and then from her: liquor must be drunk, but desire delights at a glance.
links.quoteA: It can’t delight those who merely see, as desire does
links.quoteB: toddy can’t do this, but desire can

links.reason: She answers the same village gossip twice: they say he has left her, but they cannot see him in her heart or in her dreams.
links.quoteA: This town says he lives apart from me
links.quoteB: They say he left me in waking life

links.reason: What a service is worth lies not in the act but in the person it reaches: the worth of the guest in one, of those who received it in the other.
links.quoteA: It is measured by the worth of the guest
links.quoteB: It is the worth of those who received it

links.reason: Hard as a good man’s poverty is, wealth held by the wrong people ranks lower still, whether they are fools or got it dishonourably.
links.quoteA: far worse is riches in the hands of the fool
links.quoteB: The indigence of the worthy is better far than wealth that is amassed by dishonourable means.

links.reason: Beauty of body counts for nothing alone: a clay image without understanding in one, no addition to the worth of character in the other.
links.quoteA: no better than the beauty of an image of clay
links.quoteB: the comeliness of the body addeth nothing

links.reason: Her reserve does not save her: desire breaks out of hiding into the open, whatever she had prided herself on.
links.quoteA: It breaks out of hiding into the open
links.quoteB: Now my desire has gone past hiding, out into the public square

links.reason: Nothing, each declares, is greater than a woman holding firm, whether in chastity or in not riding the palmyra stalk under a sea of desire.
links.quoteA: What is greater than a woman, if she has the strength called chastity?
links.quoteB: Nothing is greater than a woman

links.reason: The joy of desire is a sequence, not a state: the sulk first, then the embrace that ends it.
links.quoteA: Sulking, making up and coming together
links.quoteB: the joy of sulking is the embrace that ends it

links.reason: Losing a fool as a friend is a gain: plain gain in one and, with irony, very sweet in the other, because the end brings no pain.
links.quoteA: to give up the friendship of fools and get clear of them
links.quoteB: When it ends, it brings no pain at all

links.reason: Fear is the mark of good sense here, not weakness: the worthy flee what the evil ignore, and the wise fear what fools rush into.
links.quoteA: The evil fear not the folly called sin: but the worthy flee from it.
links.quoteB: it is the part of the wise to fear what ought to be feared

links.reason: She tells the same small defeat twice: she set out to sulk, and her heart had already gone to him.
links.quoteA: I went off meaning to sulk. I saw my heart was ready to join him
links.quoteB: I went there to sulk, my friend, but my heart forgot that and went to join him

links.reason: A village tree shows what a rich man’s wealth is to his neighbours: fruit for all when he has heart, poison when he is unloved.
links.quoteA: a fruit-tree in the middle of the village
links.quoteB: the fruiting of the poison tree in the midst of the village
